# Synthetic MCP transport controls

These are synthetic precision and output-size controls, not observations of GAAP
business activity. No currency or financial-unit claim applies to their numbers.
The original 475-row CSV and reviewed business definitions remain unchanged.

The standard core/ontology/mapping documents derive from the reviewed
`docs/research/ossie-req-001/proposed-definitions/` threshold-10 bundle. The core
adds Integer `ordinal`, String `payload` and `SUM(ordinal)`; ontology and mapping
add the corresponding scalar relationships. Descriptions are synthetic; the
threshold rule and existing names remain for the shared production templates.
The local manifest binds the exact new document bytes by SHA-256.

`numeric-rows.sql` contains six literal rows: adjacent cent values above 2^53,
a DECIMAL(38,2) value, signed BIGINT boundaries, negatives and NULL. The verifier
compares native frozen objects and SUM with independent text/BigInt expectations,
then compares MCP raw numeric tokens and ordinary JSON number decoding separately.
Native integer SUM widens to HUGEINT; the positive-row sum exceeds BIGINT.

The large fixture is generated by `scripts/verify_population_transport.ts`:
10,000 unique IDs, cents 0..9,999, ordinal 0..9,999, and the five-character payload
`中`, quote, backslash, newline, tab repeated 160 times. Decimal import uses
integer quotient/remainder to construct exact text. Expected totals are COUNT
10,000, SUM 499,950.00 and integer SUM 49,995,000. Every object field and group is
checked; hashes and actual content/JSON-RPC byte counts are recorded without
embedding the entire large response in the report. Membership/order is checked
as an ID set, not by assuming row order.

The verifier also links empty objects/groups to compile metadata under fixed
startup with no reload tool, checks empty aggregate semantics, and confirms
10,001-row and over-16-MiB canonical captures refuse without replacing the old
batch. These are input-load limits, not measured output maxima or memory bounds.
